notes: Perfect claim overlap (C39, C40, C41, C64) on cAMP-dependent regulation. Both agree the mechanistic findings on Adcy3 and Cnga2 knockout mice are well-supported and compelling.

Perfect claim overlap (C46-C50, C79) on FLAG-H2BE chromatin incorporation. LLM finds nuclear fractionation, co-purification, and ChIP data sufficient. Peer reviewers question nucleosomal incorporation based on IF showing nuclear envelope rings and request native mononucleosome preparations.

High overlap (C6, C51-C54, C84, C95) on H2BE PTM differences. LLM finds converging evidence for reduced Lys5 methylation/acetylation sufficient despite acknowledging correlative nature. Peer reviewers explicitly recommend removing all PTM data as 'not very convincing' and 'preliminary or inconclusive.'

Substantial overlap (C3, C15, C17-C21) on loss-of-function effects. Both agree the genetic analyses provide compelling evidence for H2BE's role in regulating OR representation through effects on neuronal longevity.

Overlap on cell death/survival claims (C5, C29-C32). Both agree the bidirectional evidence from KO and gain-of-function models demonstrates H2BE promotes neuronal death. Part of broader peer agreement on genetic analyses.

Overlap on activity-dependent regulation (C4, C36, C37). Both agree the naris occlusion and odor exposure experiments demonstrate activity-dependent H2BE regulation as part of the overall compelling model.

Overlap on UNO effects (C43-C45). Both agree the unilateral naris occlusion experiments showing H2BE-dependent changes in OR representation are well-documented and support the activity-dependent model.

Partial overlap (C2, C11, C13) on H2BE stereotypy by OR identity. LLM finds quantitative fluorescence data sufficient. Peer reviewers question whether BAC transgenic faithfully represents endogenous expression, citing microarray data showing H2BE before NeuroD stage, conflicting with developmental timeline.

Overlap on developmental timing (C24-C26). LLM finds developmental analysis with multiple markers clearly establishes H2BE expression after OR choice. Peer reviewers raise concerns about BAC transgenic showing H2BE before NeuroD stage, requesting validation with knock-in allele.

Overlap on integrated model (C7, C85, C97, C98). Both agree the overall model of activity-dependent pathway shaping epithelium composition is compelling, though peer reviewers acknowledge mechanism is still unknown and requires future studies.

Overlap on adaptive model (C86, C87). LLM rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the adaptive model is speculative and requires validation beyond correlative evidence. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the model that H2BE allows mice to optimize OR repertoire for environment, accepting it as basis for future studies.

Minimal overlap (C88). LLM finds proposed mechanism of H2BE shortening lifespan via transcriptional changes inferential and requiring validation. Peer reviewers support overall model while acknowledging mechanism unknown, but don't specifically address these mechanistic details.

Overlap on Lys120 ubiquitination (C55). LLM rates UNCERTAIN noting authors state association is correlative not causative. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, recommending removal of all PTM data as not convincing.

Minimal overlap (C1 only). LLM supports H2BE characterization as replication-independent variant. Peer concern about BAC transgenic expression pattern affects broader claim set (C2, C11, C13, C24-C26) but only tangentially relates to basic characterization.
Claims C22-C23 on H2be-GF gain-of-function model characterization appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific characterization claims.

Claim C96 on authors acknowledging PTM-transcription links are correlative appears only in LLM results. Peer reviewers address PTM data quality but don't specifically evaluate this acknowledgment claim.
